title: INDIA Bloc Seeks All-Party Meeting After Manipur Civilian Killings
excerpt: A delegation led by former Chief Minister Okram Ibobi Singh urged Chief Minister Khemchand Singh to convene all parties after three firewood collectors were killed in Imphal East; the Chief Minister assured them the demand would be looked into.
body:
• An INDIA bloc delegation led by former Chief Minister Okram Ibobi Singh met Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh in Imphal on Tuesday and urged him to convene an all-party meeting after three civilians were killed in Imphal East.
  • Khemchand Singh gave the delegation a patient hearing and assured them the matter would be looked into, his office said; no date for an all-party meeting has been announced.
  • The demand follows Monday's ambush of Meitei firewood collectors near Nongshum, protests that brought two bodies to the Chief Minister's residence, and a 48-hour statewide shutdown.
  • What this means on the ground: shops, banks, schools and transport stayed shut across Manipur on Tuesday under the shutdown, while essential services were exempted and flights operated normally.

An opposition INDIA bloc delegation led by former Manipur Chief Minister Okram Ibobi Singh met Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh on Tuesday and urged him to convene an all-party meeting on the security situation after three civilians were killed in Imphal East district, according to NDTV.

The meeting, held at the Chief Minister's Secretariat in Babupara, is the new political development in a crisis that began with Monday's killings. The delegation included Congress Legislature Party leader K. Meghachandra Singh, Lok Sabha MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam and MLA Okram Surjakumar, along with leaders of other INDIA bloc parties.

Khemchand Singh said the representatives had urged him to convene an all-party meeting in view of the prevailing situation. "I gave them a patient hearing and assured them that the matter would be looked into," he said, adding that the discussion covered maintaining peace and making collective efforts to restore normalcy in the state.

"How long can we tolerate this? Day by day, people are killing each other."

— Okram Ibobi Singh, former Manipur Chief Minister, speaking to IANS

Ibobi Singh told IANS the delegation met the Chief Minister at 11 a.m. and proposed a number of suggestions, including that all-party meetings be used to discuss the law and order situation as they were during earlier Congress rule, and that the Chief Minister's office arrange, if necessary, a meeting with the Prime Minister or the Home Minister for a delegation from the state.

The killings behind the demand

The delegation's visit followed the killing of three Meitei civilians by armed men at Nongshum in Imphal East. Reuters reported that unidentified militants opened fire on 14 Meitei villagers who were cutting and transporting firewood. Senior police official Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo said three people succumbed to bullet injuries and others were being treated. Meitei groups blame Kuki militants for the attack, which Kuki groups deny, Reuters said.

https://x.com/ndtv/status/2112477980492693590

The killings set off protests in Imphal, where grieving villagers and family members placed two bodies at the gates of the Chief Minister's residence. A wave of incidents across Imphal East and Thoubal districts over 24 hours killed four people in total, injured several others and left three people reported missing, according to reporting on Monday's security meetings.

The government's response so far

Before Tuesday's opposition meeting, Khemchand Singh chaired a meeting of legislators from the ruling National Democratic Alliance on Monday. The Chief Minister's Office said the legislators unanimously condemned the Imphal East incident in the strongest terms and directed police and security forces to apprehend the perpetrators immediately, in reporting carried by IANS via The Freedom Press. The Chief Minister also met a Joint Action Committee formed over a separate killing and assured its representatives their demands would be looked into and action taken as per law.

On the streets, a 48-hour statewide shutdown called by the Native People's Committee Manipur, alongside a 32-hour shutdown called by Iramdam Kanba Lup, crippled normal life on Tuesday, ANI reported via LatestLY. Shops, markets, banks, private offices and educational institutions closed, public and private transport was largely suspended, and inter-state road transport stopped, while medical and other essential services were exempted and airline services operated normally.

What happens next

Manipur's Meitei and Kuki communities have fought sporadically since May 2023 over economic benefits and job quotas, Reuters noted, though fighting had calmed in recent months and the last reported death in violence between the two communities before this week was in January. Whether an all-party meeting happens, and when, is now the immediate test. No date has been announced, and the opposition's request to take the issue to the Prime Minister or Home Minister through the Chief Minister's office remains unanswered in the public statements so far.
